footer.attribution: All images are from Wikimedia Commons under their respective licenses. All content is sourced from Nias Wikipedia and Wikibooks. Some pages may contain errors or are still being worked on and are not yet finalised. WikiNias volunteers are working hard to bring you all this content for free, and they would be grateful if you could join them in building the wiki, as the motto says, "Moroi khöda, soguna khöda ba soguna khö ndraonoda miföna".

heritage.architecture_desc: Delve into the ancestral heritage of the Nis people in building their eartquake-resistant traditional wooden houses.
heritage.arts_desc: Traditional Nias arts: songs, dances, hoho speeches, musical instruments, carvings, and ornaments.
heritage.clothing_desc: Traditional Nias attire, its colors and motifs, as well as other accessories.
heritage.introduction_desc: The background why the Nias Heritage project was necessary: reclaiming the Nias narrative shaped by foreign misinterpretation that the younger Nias generation is not aware of anymore.
heritage.megalith_desc: Carved stone monuments (behu and daro-daro) erected to commemorate ancestors and mark social status within the village.
heritage.origin_desc: DNA and archaeological research reveal the origins of the Nias people as part of an ancient human migration from the Asian continent that traversed the Indonesian archipelago.

home.heritage_subtitle: Uncover the uniqueness of Nias: from megaliths and traditional architecture to vibrant dances, attire, and the fascinating history of Ono Niha.
home.interactive_subtitle: Immerse yourself in the Nias language with interactive crosswords and lessons, connect with the community, or admire our curated gallery of arts and culture.
home.library_subtitle: Deep dive into Nias language and culture: practice proverbs and Hoho speeches, explore folklores and songs, or study the Nias Bible.
home.purpose_desc: Nias Heritage is a curated digital repository dedicated to preserving, documenting, and showcasing the rich history, oral traditions, cultural artifacts, and language of Nias Island, Indonesia. It challenges the dominant narrative — rooted in the misinterpretations of early explorers and visitors — that has long shaped modern understanding of Nias culture, religion, and philosophy.
